weights.csoNote: Stays UNCONDITIONAL must-not-miss. The whole point of this complaint: ~1 in 4 posterior-circulation strokes presents as ISOLATED dizziness, and a benign-sounding history does NOT exclude it. 'Cannot stand / walk' (truncal ataxia) and 'With focal neuro symptoms' are the capturable red flags. HINTS is the bedside discriminator (examTargets already prompt it) and outperforms early MRI in acute vestibular syndrome — but it is only valid in CONTINUOUS vertigo with nystagmus, never in episodic/positional dizziness. 'New deafness + vertigo' is weighted POSITIVE (not negative) because AICA infarction causes sudden deafness with vertigo — hearing loss does not mean peripheral.
weights.weightCitation: Kattah et al., HINTS to Diagnose Stroke in the Acute Vestibular Syndrome, Stroke 2009;40:3504-10 (HINTS more sensitive than early MRI; dangerous-HINTS 100% sensitive / 96% specific for central lesion); Machner et al., systematic review of HINTS in AVS (pooled sensitivity 95.5%, specificity 71.2%); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022), posterior circulation stroke. HIV as an independent stroke risk factor in sub-Saharan Africa.

weights.csoNote: Stays UNCONDITIONAL must-not-miss — arrhythmic presyncope is syncope's near-miss and the ECG is cheap. 'True spinning' weighted strongly against (a spinning patient is not having a Stokes-Adams attack); light-headed/faint type plus palpitations or syncope is the pattern. Rheumatic heart disease carried as a risk because of the Ugandan RHD burden (AF secondary to mitral disease).
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2018 Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of syncope (red flags, arrhythmic presyncope); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022), palpitation and syncope.

weights.csoNote: Stays UNCONDITIONAL must-not-miss — capillary glucose is a bedside test that costs nothing and is already in the map's examTargets; EVERY dizzy patient gets a glucose. Malaria carried as a risk: hypoglycaemia is a WHO severe-malaria criterion (and quinine itself provokes hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia), which matters more in Uganda than in the source textbooks.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines for malaria (2023), severe malaria criteria incl. hypoglycaemia (<2.2 mmol/L) and quinine-induced hypoglycaemia; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (diabetes, hypoglycaemia); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022).

weights.csoNote: Commonest single cause of true vertigo, hence basePrior 3. Female predominance ~2:1 and rising incidence with age are consistently reported. Diagnosis is Dix-Hallpike, treatment is Epley — but the negative weights matter as much as the positive ones: continuous vertigo, focal signs, or inability to stand are NOT BPPV and must push the central causes up instead.
weights.weightCitation: AAO-HNSF Clinical Practice Guideline: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (Update), Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 2017;156(3S):S1-S47; Bárány Society ICVD criteria for BPPV; von Brevern et al., epidemiology of BPPV (age and female predominance).

weights.csoNote: Acute vestibular syndrome (continuous vertigo over days) — the ONLY setting in which HINTS is valid, and the exact presentation that a posterior-circulation stroke mimics; never label neuritis without the HINTS/central sweep. Hearing loss weighted POSITIVE here (labyrinthitis involves the cochlea; neuritis spares it). UGANDA CAPTURE GAP: chronic suppurative otitis media is a locally common cause of suppurative labyrinthitis and there is no otological-history / ear-discharge capture token — recommend adding one; until then this dx rides the continuous+spinning+hearing-loss pattern only.
weights.weightCitation: Bárány Society ICVD consensus (acute vestibular syndrome / vestibular neuritis); Kattah et al., Stroke 2009 (HINTS validity restricted to AVS); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022), vestibular disorders.

weights.csoNote: Confirmed at the bedside by lying/standing BP (already an examTarget) — a drop of >=20 mmHg systolic or >=10 mmHg diastolic within 3 minutes of standing. Very common and very treatable (drug review, fluids); antihypertensives and diabetic autonomic neuropathy are the dominant drivers.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2018 Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of syncope (orthostatic hypotension definition and management); Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (hypertension, drug review); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022).

weights.csoNote: THE Uganda-calibrated entry, and the biggest departure from Western sources. In the Mulago medical emergency ward 64.6% of adult admissions were anaemic, and DIZZINESS was significantly associated with anaemia (OR 1.64, 95% CI 1.07-2.44) — hence basePrior 3, where a UK/US text would give 1. Independently associated with malaria, HIV and heavy hookworm infection. CONDITIONAL pin (gated on pallor / overt bleeding / a haemolysis-or-blood-loss risk) rather than unconditional, so it does not alarm-flood every dizzy patient — but the gate is deliberately wide and includes 'pallor', which the general exam already captures (aliased to 'conjunctival pallor'). Severe anaemia is a transfusion decision, not a reassurance: check Hb.
weights.weightCitation: Kiggundu et al. / Mulago medical emergency ward, Prevalence and morphological types of anaemia and hookworm infestation in the medical emergency ward, Mulago Hospital, Uganda (S Afr Med J / SAJ 2009) — anaemia 64.6%, dizziness OR 1.64; Bahendeka et al., PLOS ONE 2013 — anaemia in older rural Ugandans 20.3%, independently associated with malaria (OR 3.49), HIV (OR 2.17), heavy hookworm (OR 3.45); WHO haemoglobin thresholds for anaemia; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (anaemia).

weights.csoNote: UGANDA-SPECIFIC and routinely missed. Injectable aminoglycosides are given for at least six months under Ugandan DR-TB guidelines; streptomycin and gentamicin are preferentially VESTIBULOTOXIC (imbalance and oscillopsia, often WITHOUT the patient noticing hearing loss), while amikacin/kanamycin are mainly cochleotoxic. Reported ototoxicity incidence 28-37% generally, up to 57% permanent SNHL in a South African MDR-TB cohort and 20% in a Ghanaian TB cohort; a Ugandan DR-TB cohort found substantial hearing loss. Add quinine, furosemide and sedating antihypertensives. CAPTURE GAP (why needsCsoInput): there is NO current-medication or ototoxic-drug token — 'tuberculosis'/'TB contact' are only a proxy for being on an injectable, and renal impairment (which raises aminoglycoside levels) is captured only as CKD. Recommend a medication-review token; until then this dx rides the hearing-loss/tinnitus/unsteady pattern plus those proxies.
weights.weightCitation: Jiang, Karasawa & Steyger / 'Re-telling the story of aminoglycoside ototoxicity: tales from sub-Saharan Africa' (2024) — vestibulotoxic vs cochleotoxic profiles, 28-37% incidence, up to 57% in SA MDR-TB; Hearing loss among patients on treatment for drug-resistant tuberculosis in Uganda, South Sudan Medical Journal 2021; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 / Uganda National TB and Leprosy Programme DR-TB regimens; Davidson's 24th ed (2022), drug-induced vestibulopathy.

weights.csoNote: PIN DELIBERATELY GATED ON FEVER, NOT ON ENDEMIC RESIDENCE. 'malaria-endemic residence/travel' is near-universal in Uganda, so gating the pin on it would fire for every dizzy patient and destroy the signal — it is kept as a scoring risk but NOT as a pin gate; the pin needs fever/rigors or a recorded malaria diagnosis. Dizziness is not itself a WHO severe-malaria criterion: it arrives via severe anaemia, hypoglycaemia and prostration, which is exactly why those three sit alongside it in this differential. Any febrile dizzy patient in Uganda gets an mRDT/blood slide. CALIBRATION: the non-febrile drivers (light-headedness, pallor) are deliberately held at +1 so that malaria cannot reach the Leading tier in an AFEBRILE patient — pallor is shared ground with anaemia, and without this malaria out-ranked the correct dx on pallor alone.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines for malaria (2023), severe malaria criteria (severe anaemia, hypoglycaemia, prostration); Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (malaria — test before treat, mRDT/microscopy); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022).

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on advanced HIV / immunosuppression / TB — WHO's instruction is to have a LOW THRESHOLD for suspecting cryptococcal meningitis in advanced HIV disease. Headache is present in ~99% and neck stiffness in only ~70%, so a normal neck does not exclude it; dizziness, cerebellar ataxia and syncope are recognised presenting features, and the unsteady/cannot-stand pattern is the capturable one. TB MENINGITIS shares this gate, this presentation and the same action — do the LP (CrAg, India ink, CSF) — and is not carried as a separate entry to avoid clutter; the CSO may wish to split it. Serum/CSF CrAg plus WHO's single-high-dose liposomal amphotericin B regimen (validated in a trial including Uganda) is the pathway.
weights.weightCitation: WHO Guidelines for diagnosing, preventing and managing cryptococcal disease among adults, adolescents and children living with HIV (2022) — low threshold in advanced HIV disease, CrAg screening, single-high-dose L-AmB (AMBITION trial incl. Uganda); WHO guidelines on the management of advanced HIV disease (2022); ASTRO-CM Ugandan cohort (ophthalmic/neurological signs in HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis).

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on an exertional trigger or a known valve lesion. EXERTIONAL light-headedness or syncope is a hard red flag — it means the cardiac output cannot rise, and the next event may be sudden death; it must never be discharged as 'dizziness'. UGANDA: rheumatic heart disease keeps the pre-test probability of a significant valve lesion far above the Western age-related-calcific pattern, and in RHD the lesion presents decades earlier — hence the modest (not decisive) age prior. Examine for a murmur and echo.
weights.weightCitation: ESC/EACTS 2021 Guidelines for the management of valvular heart disease; ESC 2018 syncope guidelines (exertional syncope/presyncope as a high-risk feature); World Heart Federation criteria for echocardiographic diagnosis of RHD; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (rheumatic heart disease).

weights.csoNote: Kept SEPARATE from Orthostatic hypotension deliberately: the postural drop is the same sign but the cause and the action differ — this one is corrected with fluids/ORS and by treating the losses (diarrhoeal illness, vomiting, sepsis, hyperglycaemic osmotic diuresis), not by stopping antihypertensives. The CSO may prefer them merged; flagged because the overlap will make both appear together in the ranking. CALIBRATION: light-headedness held at +2 so the postural trigger ('On standing', +3) is what carries this dx to Leading, rather than presyncope-type dizziness alone.
weights.weightCitation: Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023 (diarrhoeal disease, dehydration assessment and ORS); WHO ORS / management of acute diarrhoea; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022), fluid and electrolyte disturbance.

weights.csoNote: One of the commonest causes of RECURRENT spontaneous vertigo, and habitually missed because the vertigo and the headache need not coincide. Bárány/IHS criteria need >=5 episodes lasting 5 min to 72 h PLUS a migraine history PLUS migrainous features in >=50% of episodes — the EMR captures NEITHER episode count NOR an ICHD-conformant migraine history, so this entry can only ever be suggestive; 'known migraine' is the proxy. Female predominance is well established. No Ugandan prevalence data found — the basePrior is extrapolated from international series and needs CSO calibration. Overlaps heavily with Meniere's early on. CALIBRATION: 'Triggered by head movement, brief' is weighted -2 because vestibular migraine episodes last 5 min to 72 h; without it, a textbook BPPV capture (brief + positional + spinning) pushed vestibular migraine to Leading alongside BPPV.
weights.weightCitation: Lempert et al., Vestibular migraine: diagnostic criteria — consensus document of the Barany Society and the International Headache Society (J Vestib Res 2012; updated 2022); ICHD-3 appendix criteria A1.6.6; Bárány Society ICVD consensus documents.

weights.csoNote: The defining quartet is episodic vertigo lasting 20 minutes to 12 hours WITH documented low-to-mid-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, plus fluctuating aural fullness/tinnitus in the affected ear — so 'Aural fullness' carries the heaviest weight as the most specific capturable token. NOTE: two of its strongest tokens ('Aural fullness', 'Minutes to hours') are dizziness-catalog displays rather than vocabulary-list tokens — they DO fire, but the CSO should confirm the wording. Formal diagnosis needs audiometry, which is not routinely available; no Ugandan prevalence data found, so basePrior 1 is conservative and needs calibration. Do not diagnose Meniere's without excluding vestibular migraine.
weights.weightCitation: Lopez-Escamez et al., Diagnostic criteria for Meniere's disease — consensus of the Barany Society, the Japan Society for Equilibrium Research, EAONO, AAO-HNS and the Korean Balance Society (J Vestib Res 2015;25:1-7); Bárány Society ICVD consensus documents.

weights.csoNote: A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION and the one entry in this file that is dangerous if it ranks too early — it is deliberately given basePrior 1 with strong negative weights on focal signs and hearing loss so it cannot outrank a central or cardiac cause. PPPD is non-spinning unsteadiness/dizziness present most days for >=3 months, worse on standing, in motion, or with complex visual patterns, and it typically FOLLOWS an acute vestibular event (neuritis, BPPV, vestibular migraine) rather than replacing it. CAPTURE GAP: the >=3-month duration and the visual-motion provocation have no token; 'Chronic over 3 weeks' is the nearest available and understates the criterion. Never surface as a label before glucose, Hb, ECG and the central sweep are done.
weights.weightCitation: Staab et al., Diagnostic criteria for persistent postural-perceptual dizziness (PPPD) — consensus document of the Bárány Society (J Vestib Res 2017;27:191-208); Bárány Society ICVD consensus documents.
